subject: Food Science
title: Organic vs. Conventional Safety
description: A 60-second lesson on Organic vs. Conventional Safety.

hook.text: Organic food sales hit $63 billion in 2021. But is organic food actually safer to eat than conventional food?

buildup.text: Organic farming limits synthetic pesticides and antibiotics. It uses natural alternatives—copper sulfate, neem oil, composting.

discovery.text: Organic produce has lower pesticide residues but is not pesticide-free. Natural pesticides are used and some leave residues.

twist.text: Organic produce has higher rates of microbial contamination in some studies—animal manure fertilizer can introduce E. coli.

climax.text: FDA testing shows both organic and conventional foods are safe. The pesticide residue levels on both are well below safety limits.

punchline.text: Organic uses fewer synthetics. Conventional stays under limits. Both are safe to eat.

quiz.question: Is organic produce completely free of pesticides?
options: No—organic farming uses natural pesticides that can leave residues
Only imported organic produce has pesticides
